context: Joseph deposits Rand into a savings account when his son is a given age; the account earns simple interest at a fixed annual rate, and when the son is older the balance is stated. The number of years must be found from the two ages, and then the rate.
stem: When his son was ${=a1}$ years old, Joseph deposited $\text{R{=P}}$ into a savings account. Simple interest was used, and when his son was ${=a2}$ years old the balance in the account had grown to $\text{R{=A}}$. Calculate the rate at which the money was invested. Give the rate as a percentage per year, written as a number without the % sign. It works out exactly, so no rounding is needed.
solution: Work out for how many years the money was invested: $n={=a2}-{=a1}={=n}$ years.
The interest is simple, so use $A=P(1+in)$ and make $i$ the subject: $\begin{aligned}A&=P(1+in)\\\frac{A}{P}&=1+in\\\frac{A}{P}-1&=in\\\frac{\frac{A}{P}-1}{n}&=i\end{aligned}$
Write $i$ as a percentage: $i={=idec}\times100={=rr}\%$ per year.
So the money was invested at a simple interest rate of ${=rr}\%$ per annum.
notes: Standard tier, modelled on ex9-1-8 (Joseph, R5000 at the son's fifth birthday, R18000 at 21, 16.25%). The extra step the book uses is that n has to be found from the two ages (a2 - a1, between 6 and 18 years), and the rate is not a whole percent: it is a multiple of 0.25% that is never whole (2.25 to 9.75). P is a multiple of 400, so gain = (P/400)*q*n is an integer and A is a whole number of Rand; the second constraint checks that i is exactly q/400. rr and idec are formatted strings so the answer shows 3.25 or 3.5 with no trailing zeros, and the worked i shows its exact decimal (0.0325 or 0.035). The stem tells the solver the rate works out exactly and to give a bare percentage number, so a blind solver does not round or answer 0.0325. No misconceptions are catalogued for this objective and the family is numeric, so there are no distractors. The book's rounded-to-one-decimal questions (ex9-1-9, 9-1-10, 9-1-11, 9-7-4, 9-7-5) and the hire-purchase twist (9-7-25) are left to the book as the advanced tier.
